featured_reviews.name: Burjiz
featured_reviews.review_text:
Stopped by at Cafe Darayush for lunch and had a pleasant experience.

The cafe has been around since 1965, and it’s recently been renovated and well maintained. The decor and photo frames add character without feeling overdone.

Ordered the Chorizo sandwich and the Chicken Mayo Toastie. Both were very good. Fresh ingredients, nicely balanced flavours, and you can tell things are made in-house. The bread was crisp, fillings were generous, and everything tasted thoughtfully put together.

Had a friendly chat with the owner as well. He mentioned they regularly update the menu and draw inspiration from different cuisines abroad, which keeps things interesting for repeat visits.

Overall, a nice spot around Grant Road (W) if you’re looking for quality sandwiches in a cosy setting. Would come back to try more.

This place was on our list of must visit South Indian restaurants.
We had to look around a bit as Google Maps dropped us off a little before and the restaurant sign wasn't visible from there.
The food was decent, although it didn’t quite live up to the expectations set by the reviews. I'm glad we got to check it out for ourselves.
We ordered,
1. Benne Masala Dosa - Ok
2. Ghee Podi Idli - Good
3. Garlic Mulbagal Dosa - Good (Most places in Mumbai that promise a Benne end up giving you a Mulbagal-esque dish although the ingredients are not all the same)
4. Filter Coffee - Not good
5. Wada - Ok

The heart shaped benne on the dosa was a nice, cute touch.
The interiors were minimalist and you could tell that a lot of thought had gone into it. I only wish the floor were clean. There were quite a few poeple there who you could tell were regulars which was nice to see.
Good luck!

featured_reviews.name: Amrutjyoti Shinde
featured_reviews.review_text: Heard a lot about this place from reels, and was not disappointed. Went with 3 friends around 3:30 pm on 14th Feb. It was not crowded at all. Started with the Iced Filter Coffee, was a little watered down, but you can always ask for more coffee concoction. Then the Goli Bhaji and Mangalore Buns were absolutely delicious, not too sweet, perfectly balancing the sweetness with the coconut chutney. Then we got 4 different doses, and the Ghee Podi Benne Masala Dosa (jain) was the bestseller for a reason. First bite was heavenly and comforting, and the masala was made of raw banana, and was in sufficient quantity. The dosa was only so flavorful, there was no need of sambar or chutney. If you take regular dosa, you get an additional tomato garlic chutney. My friend ordered the Mulbagal Dosa, which they claim to have started the 1st time in Mumbai. Some might say you would get doses at cheaper prices elsewhere, but their price reflects their commitment to perfection and love towards serving people. I will definitely visit this place again..!!

Ambience & Space
Cafe Coffee Day is spacious and well laid out, making it a comfortable place to sit, relax, or catch up with friends. The large size of the café adds to the ease and openness of the overall experience.

Interior Condition (Scope for Improvement)
While the space is good, the café does need a bit of interior renovation. Some sections of the walls appeared decayed, and it was quite noticeable. A refresh would definitely enhance the overall look and bring the interiors up to date.

Coffee Experience
I had a cappuccino, and it tasted good—smooth, well-balanced, and enjoyable. It delivered the familiar Café Coffee Day quality that coffee lovers appreciate.

Merchandise Purchase
Along with the coffee, I also purchased a bottle from their merchandise collection. It was a nice addition and a good takeaway item for regular use.

Staff & Service
The staff was very helpful, polite, and attentive. Their friendly approach made the visit more pleasant and hassle-free.

Final Verdict
Overall, it was a good experience at Cafe Coffee Day. With some interior renovation and upkeep, this café can feel much fresher while continuing to offer good coffee, helpful staff, and a comfortable space.

featured_reviews.review_text:
A Coffee Pilgrimage to The Craftery by Subko

The Hunt: Finding this place is a bit of a treasure hunt. Hidden deep within the industrial by-lanes of Byculla, the journey through the gritty, winding streets only adds to the payoff. It feels like a well-kept secret that you have to earn.
The Senses: The moment you step through the doors, the city noise vanishes. You are immediately woken up by a powerful, beautiful symphony of aromas—freshly roasted coffee beans, warm cookies, and artisanal breakfast goodies straight from the oven.
The Brew: This isn't just a cafe; it’s a full-blown coffee experience. Our group explored a variety of their manual and iced brews:
Ratnagiri Estate (Medium Roast): Exceptionally clean and balanced—easily the highlight for anyone who appreciates estate-specific Indian coffee.
Iced Long Blacks & Lattes: Perfectly pulled shots; the quality of the bean really shines through even when chilled.
The Atmosphere: It’s a nice, cosy space that feels both professional and inviting. Watching the "craft" happen while you sip your drink makes it feel special.
Verdict: If you’re a coffee purist or just looking for a breakfast spot that feels like an escape, make the trip. The "hunt" for the entrance is absolutely worth the reward inside.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Great Spot for an Unbeatable Cup of Chai and Quick Munchies

If you're looking for a solid place to grab a classic cutting chai or a quick evening snack in Parel, Chaos Control Cafe is a fantastic choice. Located right in the thick of the action, this spot has become immensely famous among the younger crowd, college students, and office folks looking to unwind. The vibe here is always energetic and buzzing.
The absolute star of the show here is their tea. They serve an amazing, deeply flavorful Kolkata-style chai in traditional clay kulhads that hits the spot every single time. Paired with their unique snack options like the Varanasi Toast or Bun Maska, it makes for a perfect, pocket-friendly evening ritual. However, a quick word of advice: if you are a hard-core coffee lover, this might not be the place for you. Their coffee simply doesn't match up to the brilliant standards of their chai, so it's best to stick to the tea menu.
As for the ambiance, it's a very small outlet, so indoor sitting is highly limited. In true Mumbai fashion, they have cleverly converted the adjacent side street into an open-air sitting area. It is a prime example of a typical, resourceful Mumbai jugad—sitting under the open sky amidst the city's chaotic energy. While it might not offer a premium, air-conditioned cafe experience, it completely works for a casual hangout with friends.
Overall, for a great cup of tea, tasty quick bites, and a lively neighbourhood atmosphere, it's highly recommended. Just skip the coffee and enjoy the street-side vibe!

featured_reviews.name: Vishwesh Ranadive
featured_reviews.review_text:
Cafe Trofima, Shivaji Park, Dadar, Mumbai

Cafe Trofima, located near the bustling Shivaji Park in Dadar, has garnered attention as a popular hangout spot, but it falls short of the hype for several reasons.

Food

The menu boasts a variety of food options, including breakfast platters, which might initially seem impressive. However, the taste of the food is compromised and does not justify the high prices. For a cafe that markets itself as a premium experience, the quality of the dishes leaves much to be desired.

Ambience and Seating

The sitting space is one of the better aspects of Cafe Trofima. Considering it is a cafe, the seating is comfortable and suitable for casual conversations or work. However, the overall ambience is just average, with no music to elevate the vibe. It lacks the warmth or charm that many would expect from a cafe in this area.

Service

The service is satisfactory but nothing extraordinary. While the staff is polite and attends to customers in a timely manner, the overall experience doesn’t stand out as memorable.

Location and Accessibility

A significant downside is the lack of parking space, which can be a hassle, especially given the busy location of Shivaji Park. Visitors arriving in their own vehicles may find it inconvenient.

Pricing

The prices are on the higher side, making it hard to justify for the quality of food and overall experience provided. While there are plenty of food options to choose from, the value for money is not reflected in the offerings.

Verdict

Cafe Trofima is overrated and doesn’t quite live up to its reputation. While it has some redeeming qualities like decent seating and satisfactory service, the compromised food taste, lack of parking, and high prices make it hard to recommend wholeheartedly. It could work as a one-time visit for those curious about its breakfast platters, but better options are available in and around the area for a more satisfying experience.

Overall Rating: 2/5

featured_reviews.review_text:
Flute 24 Hrs had a mixed dining experience overall.

The starters were quite good and flavourful. We ordered the Korean Style Chicken and Murgh Phoolzadi Kebab, both of which were enjoyable and well prepared.

However, the mains was a disappointment. We ordered the Murg Angara, and it lacked proper flavour and tasted quite off compared to the strong start from the appetizers. I also felt the recommendation for the mains could have been better.

Something unique about Flute in comparison to most other restaurants is that a 5% service fee is included and charged to the bill. This is interesting because tipping in India is optional as far as I am aware. This resulted in a modest increase in the bill of around ₹100 for the three dishes. However I would usually tip more but because the service fee was included it made little sense to top anything and felt somewhat redundant.

The service was nice as per my expectation but this practice is one which I have encountered in few restaurants and certainly is not a norm and so is something to be aware about.

The restaurant otherwise was good though but slightly priced on the premium side.

I thought some items were inappropriately priced. One small roti at ₹88 (excluding any taxes) seemed like a rip off because it averaged 3-4 rotis on just one dish so felt a bit unusual seeing ₹300 on a side dish of a basic small roti.

That said, the ambience was quite nice. The restaurant was air-conditioned, comfortable and relaxing, with an IPL match playing alongside mild instrumental music which made for a calm dining atmosphere.

Overall, good starters and ambience, but inconsistent mains and somewhat inflated pricing.

featured_reviews.name: Yogesh Gunjal
featured_reviews.review_text:
My recent dining experience was not very satisfactory. The place is quite expensive, and the portion sizes do not match the pricing. The food quality also did not meet expectations.

We ordered pesto pasta, but they did not serve even a single piece of garlic bread along with it. Usually, any standard café or restaurant provides at least one garlic bread with pasta, so this was disappointing.

We also ordered a brownie shake, but the shake had very little brownie in it. It tasted more like a basic chocolate shake with a lot of cream. Considering the price, the shake did not feel worth it.

Additionally, the restaurant charges a compulsory 7% service charge. However, there was no table service provided — the staff simply placed the food on the table and we had to serve ourselves. We ended up paying around ₹135 as service charge for just two dishes, which feels inappropriate.

Overall, I don’t think the dining experience is worth the price, and I would not recommend this place for dining.

I'm sorry to hear that your experience fell short of what we aim to provide. Your comments regarding the portion sizes, food quality, and service charge have been noted, and we are actively reviewing our menu offerings and service protocols to ensure a better experience for all our guests. We want to provide value and satisfaction at every level, and we apologize for not meeting those expectations during your visit. For further queries and reservations, please call us at 8591075473
Thank you,
Grandmamas Cafe

featured_reviews.name: Himmti Kaintura
featured_reviews.review_text: I loved the food and taste. It is a best combination of healthy and tasty food. Also a pocket friendly.  The taste  was perfect 👌. Best option for lunch  , brunch, breakfast and snacks as well.

featured_reviews.name: Mihir Shah
featured_reviews.review_text:
Mani Cafe is a bustling food joint located in the heart of Dadar, a prominent area in Mumbai. The cafe has a pleasant and inviting ambiance with indoor and outdoor seating arrangements. The interior is decorated in a modern yet rustic style with wooden decor and rustic textured walls.

The menu of the cafe mainly focuses on a wide range of dishes from the fusion cuisine, including Italian, Mexican, and Indian food with vegan and gluten-free options. The cafe is best known for its breakfast options, including waffles, pancakes, and French toasts. It also serves varieties of coffee, tea, and cold beverages.

Customers have appreciated the prompt and hospitable service offered by the staff and the overall value of the prices. Families with kids and locals frequently visit the cafe for its relaxed atmosphere.

However, some patrons have pointed out the limited options on the menu and the lack of authenticity in the dishes' flavor. The cafe's location is convenient, but the parking space is inadequate, and customers sometimes find difficulty park their vehicles nearby.

Overall, Mani Cafe offers a pleasant dining experience with a comfortable ambiance and a variety of food options from the fusion cuisine. It is a perfect spot for those looking to hang out with family and friends over coffee or a quick bite.

I met my childhood friend after 10 years and The manager kept hounding us to order something or leave because the cafe had bookings. Mind you, i had ordered and ate 3 dishes from the restaurant + 1 coffee and even that was not enough for them to let us stay and talk for half an hour.
This guy was extremely rude, made a face when i asked him to let us stay atleast 1/2 an hour.
for a customer that ate so much of food from your restaurant and got spoken to in such a rude manner that me and my friend had to pack up and leave, i would never visit again.

Now the food :
Ordered the paneer burger, homemade paneer burger has more taste. The fries that came on the side were 9 pieces in total. This wasn’t hitting so i ordered the pink pasta, bland as anything, even with oregano the pasta could not lift up in flavour. Extremely disappointing food.

My question : For a manager to come and hound us to leave cause his cafe had bookings, one would expect the cafe to be exceptional that so many people are wanting to be here but this was not the case. Staff sucks, manager sucks, meeting my friend after 10 years i wanted to spend the time talking to her and catch up but this restaurant completely and utterly failed us in every element. Cafe’s are supposed to be a comfort corner of the world where people come to share stories, exchange a good time and just be. in the middle of it if you are being hounded and pestered to order again and again and again just to stay in the cafe, sorry but your venture sucks and doesnt deserve to be called a comfort cafe.

featured_reviews.review_text:

Service was a bit slow. We had to wait even though there were free tables.

featured_reviews.name: Himanshu Kawle
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had a great experience with the Veggie Farmhouse with Chicken Thin Crust Pizza, Soya Chilli Chicken, and Harissa Grilled Chicken Steak with Garlic Mayo.
The thin crust pizza was just how I like it—crispy base, flavorful mozzarella, and perfectly balanced veggies and chicken.
The Soya Chilli Chicken used well-cooked chicken breast pieces with capsicum, onion, and spring onion, all tossed in a perfectly balanced soy sauce with the right hint of white pepper.
The Harissa Grilled Chicken Steak was nicely grilled with a tandoori touch, served with grilled veggies like broccoli, zucchini, carrots, and mashed potatoes.
Overall, the food quality was excellent and truly value for money.

featured_reviews.name: mukul chandorkar
featured_reviews.review_text: I have been a regular customer at August cafe since many years. They have recently redesigned the whole place and has made it more cozy and inviting! The food is amazing as always and special mention to Chocolate mud cake!! Literally everything on the menu is delicious and carefully crafted!

featured_reviews.name: Ajay Dogra
featured_reviews.review_text:
Stopped by August Café for breakfast and it was a lovely way to start the day — fresh food, relaxed vibe, and great coffee. Special shout-out to Bonny for warm, attentive service that made the visit even better. Will definitely return! ⭐

Edit
Came back to August Café and it was just as delightful as the first visit. Loved the mix mushroom omelette finished with truffle oil — simple, earthy and perfectly done — paired beautifully with a smooth flat white. The café was peaceful in the early morning, with lovely, unobtrusive music setting a calm mood that made the meal even more enjoyable. A great place to start the day, and once again, the service was warm and impeccable. ⭐

featured_reviews.review_text:
### **Review for Prithvi Café**
Prithvi Café is legendary for its vibe and history, but if I’m being honest, the food felt a bit overhyped. It’s a great spot to hang out, but the flavors were a hit-or-miss for me :(

So, I was leaving for out of India but just wanted to explore this cafe before leaving as I will be missing Indian food a little!
But, I kind of got disappointed with the food. To be honest the dishes I had at airport were better🥲

**The Food Breakdown:**
🌟 Egg Kheema: Just okay. It didn't quite live up to the expectations I had based on the reviews.
🌟 Butter Chicken Thali: This was a letdown. The gravy was **way too sweet**—even for Butter Chicken. It lacked that savory, spicy balance you'd expect.
🌟 Mixed Veg Paratha: One of the better items we ordered. Solid, filling, and tasted fresh.
🌟 Burger (Must Try!): The highlight of the meal. The bun isn't made of maida (refined flour), which gave it a great texture. Definitely worth a try if you want something "healthier" but tasty.
Chocolate Croissant: A decent sweet finish, but nothing groundbreaking.

**Drinks:**
We tried the Blueberry Soda and Masala Soda. Both were refreshing and served as good palate cleansers for the meal.

Go for the atmosphere and the non-maida burgers, but maybe skip the North Indian mains if you aren't a fan of sweet gravies. It's a nice place to chill, just don't expect a culinary masterpiece across the whole menu.

featured_reviews.name: The explorer
featured_reviews.review_text: Inspite of visiting a couple of times before, we've never shot pictures to upload in the review as this was a busy place that involved queue system to be seated. Our last visit was on a weekday afternoon and hence we got a table without a wait time. The seating is outdoor and the menu is pocket friendly and extensive. Most of their kitchen seems outdoor and causes fumes,sizzles and fragrances of multiple dishes being cooked. The dining is moderately under dhaded trees and thoroughly placed table fans. The menu and ordering are online while the bill can be paid once your are  about to leave. Service staff are busy but give you attention when needed. Our asked for extra plate/spoon have immediately been fulfilled. The orders once placed have also arrived quick to the table. We've been ordering from this place for years and hence have reordered most of our favorites to enjoy them fresh which include their paratha with dal makhani, red velvet brownie and cookies. Their sulemani chai and masala soda were well made too. No excessive sugars in the beverages that we ordered. Overall it was a nostalgic place for us and being able to dine without a wait time is a plus.

featured_reviews.name: Mayur Aundhakar
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited **Prithvi Café** and had a really good experience overall. The café has a beautiful, lively ambience with a chilled, artsy vibe — perfect for casual meetups or relaxed meals.

I tried quite a few dishes here:
🍽️ **Amritsari Paratha** – Nicely stuffed, flavorful, and served hot with curd and chutney. The taste was authentic and had a pleasant spicy punch without being overpowering.
🍝 **White Pasta** – Creamy, rich, and perfectly cooked. The sauce was smooth and mildly cheesy, though it could use a little more spice for those who like stronger flavors.
☕ **Hot Coffee & Filter Coffee Ice-Cream** – Both were excellent. The hot coffee was strong and aromatic, while the filter coffee ice-cream was a unique treat — a perfect balance of bitterness and sweetness.
🥭 **Mango Lassi** – Thick, fresh, and refreshing, with a real mango flavor. It paired well with the paratha and gave a nice desi touch to the meal.
🌯 **Chicken Roll** – Juicy, well-marinated, and wrapped in soft bread. Nicely spiced and filling; non-veg lovers will definitely enjoy this.

The **service** was polite and quick despite the crowd. **Pricing** is slightly on the higher side, but the taste and ambience justify it. The **outdoor seating** under trees gives a cozy, café-theatre vibe that’s hard to find elsewhere in Mumbai.

✅ **Overall:** Quite good experience — tasty food, soothing coffee, and vibrant atmosphere. A must-visit if you’re near Juhu, especially for coffee lovers and café enthusiasts

featured_reviews.name: Ameeta mehta
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Coffee Purist’s Haven in a Serene Locale.

Blue Tokai in Breach Candy is less of a typical café and more of a sanctuary for serious coffee lovers. Located on a quiet, leafy lane, it provides an escape from the city’s hustle without compromising on a world-class caffeine fix.

The Coffee & Food (4.5/5):
The coffee is, of course, the hero. I ordered a pour-over of their seasonal roast (a Kenyan) and a flat white. Both were brewed to perfection – balanced, aromatic, and showcasing the beans’ distinct notes. The baristas are knowledgeable and happy to explain the profiles. The food menu is thoughtfully curated to complement the coffee. The Avocado & Feta Toast on sourdough was fresh and satisfying, and the Almond Croissant was flaky and buttery. It’s simple, quality fare that doesn't distract from the main event.

Ambiance & Service (4/5):
The space is modern, minimalist, and flooded with natural light. The high ceilings, clean lines, and wooden accents create a calm, focused atmosphere. It’s ideal for reading, working solo, or having a quiet conversation. Service is efficient and polite, though it can feel a bit reserved – the staff are more artisans than greeters, which fits the vibe.

Considerations:

It’s a destination for coffee. If you’re looking for a full, loud brunch scene or sugary flavored lattes, this isn’t it.

Seating can be limited during peak weekend mornings, especially the coveted window spots.

Parking in Breach Candy can be a challenge; consider using a ride-share.

Verdict:
Blue Tokai Breach Candy is a gem for anyone who appreciates specialty coffee in a serene, stylish setting. It’s a place to slow down, savor your cup, and enjoy a moment of quiet productivity or reflection. You come for the exceptional coffee, and you stay for the peaceful ambiance. A definite recommend for a quality caffeine retreat.

featured_reviews.name: Pankaj
featured_reviews.review_text:
In a busy residential area, there stands Blue Tokai with a mini lawn area outside. The setting itself is a refreshing change for a claustrophobic city like Mumbai. Hopped in on a weekday after a visit to the hospital nearby as we needed a quick lunch before heading home.
Ordered a Korean bun and cheese and tomato sandwich along with an iced cappuccino.  The Korean bun was 6, and so was the sandwich. They got the iced cappuccino right as I requested it to be cold and not iced. For a sugar rush, I ordered the chocolate cookie, which was chewy and tasty enough.
